chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Muhammad ibn Yunus narrated to us, who said: Hammad ibn Isa narrated to us, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) three [days] before his death:

"Peace be upon you, O Abu al-Rayhantayn (Possessor of the Two Fragrances). I entrust you with my two fragrances from the world. Soon, your two pillars will fall, and Allah will be my deputy over you."

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, Ali said: "This is one of my two pillars that the Messenger of Allah mentioned to me." When Fatima (peace be upon her) died, Ali (peace be upon him) said: "This is the second pillar that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) mentioned."

key_terms.أَبُو الرِّيحَانَتَيْنِ: Abu al-Rayhantayn (Possessor of the Two Fragrances), a title for Ali referring to Fatima and Hasan.
key_terms.خَلِيفَتِي عَلَيْكَ: My deputy over you, indicating Ali's role as the Prophet's successor in guardianship.
key_terms.رُكْنَاكَ: Your two pillars, referring to the two key family members entrusted to Ali.
key_terms.رِيحَانَتِي مِنَ الدُّنْيَا: My two fragrances from the world, a metaphor for beloved family members.

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'two fragrances' and 'two pillars' mentioned by the Prophet to Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s intimate address to Ali as 'Abu al-Rayhantayn' (Father of the Two Fragrances), linking the title to his daughters Fatima and Hasan. Shia scholarship interprets the 'two pillars' (ruknayn) as Fatima and Hasan, whose passing marked the loss of the Prophet’s spiritual and physical support, a concept often connected to the Verse of Purification and the Verse of Mubahala.
